UserAgent.description:
Required in practice, not by the application. Cloudflare's Browser
Integrity Check reads it, and default library signatures are blocked.
Any custom string passes. Declared optional because browsers forbid
scripts from setting this header at all.
UserAgent.name: User-Agent

CloudflareRefused.description:
Not from the application. Cloudflare's Browser Integrity Check refused
the request because the `User-Agent` was a default library signature.
The body is Cloudflare's HTML, not JSON. Set any custom `User-Agent`
and the same request succeeds. `Python-urllib/3.x` presents as
Cloudflare error 1010 rather than 403.

Browser-based API explorers cannot help here: the Fetch specification
forbids scripts from setting `User-Agent`, so the browser's own value
is sent whatever is typed into the field.

Result.description:
A human-readable message, returned in Hebrew on most failures. Map
on `ErrorCode` and supply your own text rather than passing this
through to an international audience. Do not string-match on it.

ChangeContactStatusRequest.description:
Identify the contact by either `EMail` or `PhoneNo`.

One behaviour to plan for: an address that is not on the account also
answers `ErrorCode` 0. A successful call is **not** proof that the
contact existed, so do not use this as an existence check. Use
`GetContactStatus` for that.

Status.description:
Any other value answers `ErrorCode` 4 with
`Unknown value of status`.

ChangeContactStatusRequest.title: ChangeContactStatus

Status.description:
Display text, in Hebrew for the states a contact can be in. Do
not branch on it, and do not assume it is present.

StatusID.description:
| Id | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Not on this account |
| 10 | Active |
| 30 | Active, after being reactivated |
| 40 | Bounced |
| 50 | Unsubscribed |

**10 and 30 both mean mailable.**

CreateContactRequest.description:
Subscribes a contact to a named list, or updates them if they already
exist. Thirteen fields are accepted, spelled exactly as below, note
the capitalisation of `EMail` and `PhoneNo`. Omit fields you are not
sending rather than sending empty strings.

**The list is not created for you.** A list that does not exist on the
same account as the key answers `ErrorCode` 4 with
`Contact list does not exist: <name>`. Build the integration so the
user names a list they already have, and show that error as "that list
was not found on your account" rather than as a generic failure.

ContactListName.description: Must already exist on the account the key belongs to.

CreateContactRequest.title: CreateContact

ErrorCode.description:
The only reliable indicator of the outcome. Serialised as a number on
some functions and as a string on others, so normalise before
comparing.

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Success | Continue |
| 1 | Key wrong, missing or revoked | Authentication failure. **Stop. Do not retry.** |
| 3 | Application error our side, or a payload the function could not process | Retry once. If it persists, send us the tracking id in `Result`. |
| 4 | A parameter is missing or invalid, most often a list that does not exist on this account | Show the user which field or list was named in `Result`. |
| 6 | Unknown function name | Fix `f`. |

SendSingleEMailMessageRequest.description:
One email, one recipient, sent immediately.

Note what this function does **not** accept: a From address, only a
display name; no CC or BCC; no attachments; and no more than one
recipient. Check for all four before calling and fall back to your own
transport when you see one.

Body.description: HTML. Set `dir="rtl"` yourself on Hebrew content.

FromName.description: A display name only. The From address is the account's.

LinkClickCountType.description:
Optional. Omit it, or send an empty string, unless support has told
you otherwise.

ReplyToEMail.description:
**Required**, even though older documentation shows it as an empty
string. Omit it and the call answers a null reference error with
`ErrorCode` 3.

SendSingleEMailMessageRequest.title: SendSingleEMailMessage

SendSingleSmsMessageRequest.description: One SMS, one recipient, sent immediately.

FromName.description:
A sender identity already approved on the account. Until it is
approved the call answers `ErrorCode` 4 with
`The SMS sender identity is not verified`.

Two forms are accepted:

- **An alphanumeric sender name**, up to 11 characters, Latin
  letters, digits and spaces only, and it has to contain at least
  one letter. Hebrew text and digits-only values are rejected. The
  "at least one letter" rule is not expressed in the patterns
  below, because doing so needs a lookahead that several regex
  engines cannot compile; it is enforced on our side.
- **A numeric sender**, in local or E.164 form.

The 11-character limit is a GSM constraint on alphanumeric sender
IDs, not a Meser 10 limit. Support varies by destination country:
alphanumeric sender IDs are not available in the United States or
Canada, where a number is used instead.

MessageBody.description:
Hebrew is sent as Unicode, which shortens a single-part message
from 160 characters to 70. Longer messages are concatenated and
billed per part.
MessageBody.example: Your code is 481902. It expires in 5 minutes.

ToPhone.description: One recipient per call. Israeli local format or E.164.

SendSingleSmsMessageRequest.title: SendSingleSmsMessage

MessageID.description:
Returned as `0` in practice, so it is not usable as a handle for
the message, and there is no function on this gateway that reads
a message's delivery state either. If you need to trace a
specific send, keep your own identifier in the message or in
your logs.

WriteResult.description:
The answer to any of the four write functions. `MessageID` appears only
on `SendSingleSmsMessage`.

ApiKeyAuth.description:
One header carries the account key, issued per account in the Meser 10
interface under account settings, advanced settings, API settings.
There is no OAuth flow, no token exchange and no refresh, and the key
stays valid until the account owner replaces it.

Send it in the header. Never in the query string, where it lands in
server logs, browser history and referrer headers.
ApiKeyAuth.name: ApiKey

info.description:
Five functions on one endpoint, authenticated with a single header.
Intended for transactional traffic: a one-time password, an order
confirmation, a receipt, a delivery notice.

Campaigns, mailing lists, groups, reporting, attachments and user
management are not here. They are on the SOAP service at
`https://ns.mesereser.com/Services/Services.asmx?wsdl`, which exposes 61
operations and authenticates with the same key.

Documentation © Meser 10 Ltd.

## Behaviours that commonly cause integration failures

**1. HTTP 200 is returned for every outcome, including a rejected key.**
`ErrorCode` is the only reliable indicator. It is serialised as a number on
some functions and as a string on others, and we have not catalogued which
does which, so normalise before comparing on every call:
`String(body.ErrorCode) === "0"`. Coerce `StatusID` and `MessageID` the
same way rather than relying on their declared integer type.

**2. Never retry an authentication failure.** Repeated failures block the
calling IP address for several hours. The block is on the address, not the
key, so reissuing the key and trying again makes it worse, and on a shared
host it takes down every other integration sending from that address.
Treat `ErrorCode` 1 as fatal and stop.

**3. Set a User-Agent header.** The hosts sit behind Cloudflare with
Browser Integrity Check on, and it reads that header. Default library
signatures are blocked: `Java/1.8.0_241` answers 403 and
`Python-urllib/3.x` answers Cloudflare error 1010. Any custom string
passes, and the value itself does not matter. The symptom is intermittent,
because a system often has two code paths to the same endpoint and only one
of them sets the header.

**4. `Result` is a human-readable message, returned in Hebrew on most
failures.** Branch on `ErrorCode` and supply your own wording. Every
message quoted in this document is an English translation of what the
gateway returns, not the string on the wire, so do not match on it.

## Limitations

- No webhooks, so event-driven integrations poll.
- No list-reading function, so a JSON-only integration cannot offer a
  dropdown of the account's lists and has to ask for the list name. The
  SOAP `GetGroupsList` covers it.
- Date and time fields come back without timezone information. Treat them
  as Israel local time.
- No sandbox. See the `GetContactStatus` notes for testing a key without
  creating anything.

## Why the four write functions share one operation

The gateway selects its function with a query-string parameter rather than
a path, and OpenAPI allows one POST per path. So all four write functions
are one operation here, their bodies given as an `anyOf` with a named
example each. The body shape cannot be validated from the body alone -
`f` decides which schema applies, so a generated client will expose a
single method taking a body. For five separate ready-to-run requests, use
the Postman collection published alongside this file.

get.description:
The only read on the gateway, and the one function called differently:
the address goes on the query string, not in a JSON body. Every JSON
body spelling answers `email parameter is empty`. POST with an empty
body works too, as long as the parameter is on the query string; this
document models the GET form.

Only `email` is supported. A `phone` parameter is not read and returns
the same empty-parameter error.

**Branch on `StatusID`, never on `Status`,** which is display text. And
note that **two ids mean active**: a contact created through the API
returns 10, and one moved back to Active after a bounce or an
unsubscribe returns 30. Treat both as mailable or you will silently
drop reactivated contacts.

**Testing a key without side effects.** Call this function with an
address that is not on the account: a valid key answers `ErrorCode` 0
with `StatusID` 0, a rejected key answers `ErrorCode` 1, and nothing is
created either way.

post.description:
Four functions are reached this way. Pick one with the `f` query
parameter and send its body as JSON.

| `f` | What it does |
|---|---|
| `SendSingleSmsMessage` | One SMS, immediately |
| `SendSingleEMailMessage` | One email, immediately |
| `CreateContact` | Add or update a contact on a named list |
| `ChangeContactStatus` | Move a contact between Active, Unsubscribed and Bounced |

The gateway also accepts these names in other casings, and accepts GET
for them as well. This document models the canonical spelling and POST,
because that is what a request validator or a generated client can
check.
